instruction: Rotate the ramp 22.5° clockwise.
Raise the ramp until its bottom height is 0.
Keep the height. Rotate the ramp back to horizontal.
Click "Basic Shapes", then choose "Sim Lab".
Add an Axis Connector.
Drag the connector's Joint Point onto the ramp.
Connect the Joint Point to the ramp.
Rotate the Axis Connector 90° clockwise.
Use Align to place the connector at the middle of the ramp's right side.
Select the Axis Connector and open the Motor Type menu.
Set the Axis Connector's Motor Type to Servo.
Set Maximum Speed to 20 RPM to slow the ramp down.
Click Edit Interaction.
Select the 1 key in the interaction keyboard.
Choose Set Position for the 1 key.
Set the 1 key to rotate the ramp 22.5° clockwise.
Add an Axis Connector for the bat.
Use Align to place the Axis Connector at the end of the bat.
Drag the connector's Joint Point onto the bat.
Set the bat connector's Motor Type to Servo.
Keep Maximum Speed at 400 RPM. Use Motor Torque 1000 N·m, lower limit 0° and upper limit 180°.
Click Edit Interaction for the bat connector.
Select the 1 key in the interaction keyboard.
Choose Set Position for the 1 key.
Set the 1 key to rotate the bat 180° clockwise.
Select the 2 key in the interaction keyboard.
Choose Set Position for the 2 key too.
Set the 2 key to return the bat to 0°.
Click Sim Lab to test the baseball game. Start the simulation.
Press 1 to roll the ball and prepare the bat.
Press 2 at the right time to hit the ball.
Alternative launch mechanism: connect a Slider Connector to the ball stopper.
Set the Slider Connector's Motor Type to Continuous.
Assign Change Speed to the 1 key and set the speed to 200 units/s.
